query: What goal-management practices support high achievement?

per_column.name: primary_intervention_type
per_column.rationale: Strong grouping axis directly tied to 'practices' in the query. Mostly well-grounded (resource_optimization, process_redesign, marketing_sales, feedback_survey all match). But the customer-satisfaction row labeled 'training_development' is unsupported by the text which describes after-sales support and personalized interactions, indicating occasional misreading.

per_column.name: automation_lever
per_column.rationale: A binary automation flag offers a modest but real axis to compare achievement. Values in samples are all False and plausibly grounded, though the flag is somewhat redundant with the automation category of primary_intervention_type.

per_column.name: feedback_loop_included
per_column.rationale: Whether a goal embeds a feedback loop is a genuine goal-management practice relevant to the query. Grounding is reasonable, though the engagement-program/survey rows plausibly involve feedback yet were marked False, suggesting some inconsistency; still no fabrication.

per_column.name: action_specificity
per_column.rationale: Specificity of the action plan is a classic driver of goal achievement and a good modeling axis. Only two levels but non-trivial. Ratings track the text plausibly (detailed multi-part goals rated high_specific).

per_column.name: benchmark_reference
per_column.rationale: Type of benchmark (last year, previous quarter, absolute, none) is a meaningful practice axis and is directly extractable from phrases like 'compared to last quarter' or 'from 78% to 90%'. Sample values are accurate.

per_column.name: multi_lever_goal
per_column.rationale: Whether a goal uses multiple levers is a reasonable practice distinction. Grounding is mostly sound; the customer-satisfaction row (two methods) is correctly True, though some borderline judgments possible. No clear fabrication.

per_column.name: measurement_mechanism
per_column.rationale: Measurement mechanism is a useful axis, but the values appear to conflate with the existing 'metric' column and sometimes contradict the text. E.g., a premium-subscription revenue goal is labeled 'survey_score' (echoing the mismatched metric field) rather than a sales/financial measure; the customer-satisfaction ratings goal labeled 'financial_metric' is also off. Groundedness suffers.

per_column.name: time_horizon
per_column.rationale: Time horizon is a core goal-management practice and clearly extractable ('next fiscal year', 'by end of Q4', 'compared to last quarter'). NULLs for silent rows are acceptable. Sample values match text well.

per_column.name: scope_breadth
per_column.rationale: Scope breadth is a useful grouping axis, but values are often inferred beyond textual support. 'company_wide' is asserted heavily where text is silent, and the premium-subscription goal is labeled 'product_line' without clear warrant. Overconfident specifics reduce grounding.

judge.rationale: The added columns collectively provide multiple genuine, non-redundant axes (intervention type, benchmark, specificity, time horizon, scope, feedback loop) that are well aligned with the query about goal-management practices supporting achievement, giving real leverage to group and model. Groundedness is generally solid for extractive columns (benchmark_reference, time_horizon), but a few columns exhibit overconfident inference or misreading: measurement_mechanism sometimes mirrors the noisy 'metric' field and contradicts the described goal, scope_breadth asserts breadth the text does not state, and primary_intervention_type occasionally misclassifies (training_development for a support/personalization goal). These are localized hallucinations rather than pervasive fabrication, so overall groundedness remains moderate-to-good.
